summary.text: Katrina Jackson-Andrews is a Democrat member of the Louisiana State Senate representing District 34, which the legislature's member page lists as covering Concordia, East Carroll, Madison, Morehouse, Ouachita, Richland, and Tensas parishes. First elected in 2019, Katrina Jackson-Andrews chairs the Senate Select Committee on Women and Children and serves as vice chair of the Health and Welfare Committee.

paragraphs.text: According to her Senate biography, Katrina Jackson-Andrews was born and raised in Monroe, graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe, and received her J.D. from Southern University in Baton Rouge in 2004.

The biography says she came to the Legislature in 2006 as a staff attorney for the House Committee on Labor and Industrial Relations and as executive director of the Louisiana Legislative Black Caucus.
It says she won the District 16 seat in the Louisiana House in 2011, was re-elected without opposition in 2015, and was elected to Senate District 34 without opposition in August 2019.
The biography lists her as a former chair of the Louisiana Legislative Black Caucus and a former vice chair of the Democratic Caucus, and says she attends Riverside Missionary Baptist Church.
The Senate page gives Katrina Jackson-Andrews's education as a B.A. from the University of Louisiana at Monroe and a J.D. from Southern University Law Center.

The Senate page lists Katrina Jackson-Andrews's committee assignments as Health and Welfare (vice chair), Agriculture, Forestry, Aquaculture, and Rural Development, Education, Finance, Joint Legislative Committee on the Budget, and Senate Select Committee on Women and Children (chair), and caucus and delegation affiliations as Louisiana Legislative Women's Caucus (vice chair), Democratic Caucus, Louisiana Legislative Black Caucus, Louisiana Rural Caucus, and North Louisiana Legislative Delegation.
